newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Coca-Coca's Hangzhou plant expands capacity.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Coca's Hangzhou plant expands capacity.

text.p: Swire Pacific Ltd said on Monday its joint-venture Coca-Cola bottling plant in Hangzhou in eastern China had completed an extension that would increase the facility's total capacity by three fold.
The extension occupied an area of more than 50,000 square metres, it said in a statement.
Coca-Cola China Ltd said the bottler, Hangzhou BC Foods Co Ltd, has invested an additional US$20 million in the operation, which now employs about 500 people.
The plant is 60 percent owned by BC Development Co Ltd, a joint venture between Coca-Cola, Swire Beverages Ltd and China International Trust and Investment Corp.
The remaining equity is split equally between China National Cereals, Oil and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corp and Hangzhou Tea Factory.
Swire Beverages is jointly held by Swire Pacific Ltd and Coca-Cola Co.
Coca-Cola said the extension was aimed to meet increased consumer demand in the province.
